title: Currency+ and Currency History: Rates, Charts, Zoom and Pan
seoTitle: Currency+ & History Charts: Zoom and Pan Guide | Convert Plus
description: Compare multiple currencies, calculate expressions, refresh rates every minute, explore exchange-rate history and learn the two-finger chart controls available in current releases.
body:
Currency+ brings several currency comparisons into one list. Currency History adds context: a chart of how the selected exchange rate has changed over time. Use them together to compare an amount today, inspect earlier readings and keep previously loaded data available when you lose your connection.

Chart gestures are available in current releases.
The US App Store returned version 3.1.4 on 26 October 2026. The pinch, two-finger pan and reset instructions below describe the current chart controls.

Compare several currencies with one input

Open Currency+ and add the currencies you want to compare. A list might start with USD and include EUR, GBP, JPY and supported crypto such as BTC. Supported precious-metal quotes can also be added. Currency availability and quote coverage depend on the data available in the app.

Enter an amount in the active card and the other amounts update together. Tap a different amount card to make that currency your input, without rebuilding the list. The advanced calculator accepts arithmetic and brackets, so you can enter (12 × 3) + 10, calculate 46, and see the converted amounts directly. It is useful for totaling items before comparing their cost in several currencies.

Up-to-the-minute comparisons

Currency+ checks for updated rates every minute while its rates page is visible, the app is active and the device is connected. It also fetches rates when you enter the screen, and provides a manual refresh button. Look at the displayed update time to see when your data was last refreshed.

A one-minute refresh interval does not mean that every source publishes a different quote each minute. A refresh can return the same rate, and an unsuccessful update keeps the last accepted data. These are reference conversions; an actual bank or card transaction can use a different rate and include fees.

Open Currency History and choose a range

Tap the chart button beside a currency to open the selected pair’s history. Choose 1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 1 year, 5 years or all available history. Short ranges help you inspect recent movement; longer ranges show a broader picture. The amount summary uses your conversion amount, so a historical reading has a useful monetary context.

The available observations and length of history vary by pair. “All” means the history available for that pair, not a promise of an unlimited record. The Min and Max labels summarize the loaded range. Currency History is separate from automatic conversion history, which records your earlier calculations.

Read a point with one finger

Tap or drag across the chart with one finger to select an actual recorded point. The readout shows its date or time, exchange rate and converted amount. This also works after you zoom or pan: one finger inspects readings, while two fingers move the chart.

Zoom and pan

  1. Pinch to zoom. Spread two fingers to zoom in, or pinch them together to zoom out. Both the horizontal time axis and vertical exchange-rate axis scale around your fingers.
  2. Pan with two fingers. Once zoomed in, drag with two fingers to move left or right through time, or up and down through the rate range. Movement stays within the loaded chart bounds.
  3. Inspect with one finger. Tap or drag to select a reading without moving the chart.
  4. Double-tap to reset. Restore the full chart. Changing the currency pair or time range also resets the view.

Zooming changes the view, not the underlying rates. It does not fetch older observations beyond the loaded range, and the Min and Max summary continues to describe that loaded range.

Keep rates and charts available offline

Load the pairs and time ranges you need while connected. Previously loaded rates and charts can then be viewed offline. A new pair, an uncached range or a fresh quote still needs a connection. Saved rates retain their timestamp; going offline does not make them current.

On a wider iPad or an open iPhone Duo window, Currency+ can show its currency list beside the history chart, making it easier to compare an amount and inspect a rate together. For a trip, open the currencies and charts you expect to use before leaving Wi-Fi, and check their update times.

title: 7 Everyday Ways a Conversion Calculator Makes Life Easier
description: A practical unit converter can make travel, cooking, shopping, exercise, schoolwork, home projects and fuel planning easier.
body:
Measurements travel with us. A recipe uses cups, a product listing uses centimeters, a running plan uses minutes per mile, and a road trip may show fuel use in liters per 100 kilometers. A conversion calculator turns those values into units you can act on. Here are seven everyday ways to use a unit converter and money converter with more confidence.

  1. Plan a trip

    When a route, rental car or travel guide uses unfamiliar units, convert distance and fuel economy before you leave. For example, a 250 km drive at 7.2 L/100 km uses about 18 L of fuel: 250 × 7.2 ÷ 100. Convert the distance to miles if that is how your itinerary is organized. A currency converter can also help you compare a listed price in local money with your home currency. Treat the result as an estimate based on the displayed exchange rate, because a card issuer or cash desk may use a different rate and fees.

  2. Follow a recipe

    Cooking measurements mix milliliters, liters, cups, teaspoons, tablespoons, grams and ounces. Convert volume to volume or weight to weight where the ingredient and recipe specify it. A cup is a volume; a gram is a mass. There is no universal cup-to-gram number for every food because flour, sugar and chopped nuts have different densities. For repeatable baking, use a recipe’s stated mass when it gives one, and keep the ingredient the same when converting.

  3. Compare product sizes

    Online shopping often lists a screen, room accessory or parcel in inches while your tape measure uses centimeters. Convert the dimensions first, then check the whole object against the space you have. Shoe size systems also differ by region, so use a size conversion as a starting point and confirm the seller’s sizing chart before ordering.

  4. Track a workout

    Runners may see pace in minutes per kilometer or minutes per mile, while a route is shown in kilometers or miles. Convert both distance and pace to the format you use in training. Keep pace units distinct from speed: minutes per mile is time over distance, while miles per hour is distance over time.

  5. Check schoolwork

    Unit conversion is a useful way to practice ratios and dimensional reasoning. Convert a measurement, then check whether the answer got larger or smaller in the expected direction. For example, a length measured in centimeters should have a smaller numerical value when expressed in meters. Writing the units alongside the numbers helps catch misplaced decimals.

  6. Plan a home project

    Before cutting, painting or arranging furniture, translate room dimensions into one consistent unit. Length, area and volume are different quantities: a floor plan in square feet cannot be converted to square meters by applying a length factor only once. Convert each dimension, or convert the area using an area conversion, then add a sensible allowance for cuts and waste from your project plan.

  7. Understand fuel use

    Vehicle listings may compare miles per gallon with liters per 100 kilometers. These are both fuel-economy measures but their numerical direction differs: a higher mpg generally means fewer gallons per distance, while a lower L/100 km means less fuel used. Convert the measure you need and compare like with like, rather than reading the number alone.

A well-rounded conversion calculator keeps common categories—length, weight, temperature, volume, area, speed, pressure, energy and fuel—close at hand. Conversion Calculator Plus includes 72 categories and 685 units, along with favourites and history for values you return to. Its expression calculator can evaluate a calculation before or alongside a conversion. Simple and Carousel layouts offer two ways to browse. The useful habit is the same in any app: select the quantity, check the source and destination units, and read the result with its unit label.

title: Metric and Imperial Conversions: A Practical Guide
description: Convert meters, feet, kilograms, pounds and temperatures with worked examples, and learn why a US gallon differs from an Imperial gallon.
body:
Metric and Imperial measurements appear side by side in travel, recipes, product dimensions and technical manuals. A reliable unit converter helps, but understanding the relationship between units makes the result easier to check. Start by identifying the quantity, keep the unit attached to every number, and use the correct conversion for the system named in the source.

1. Convert meters to feet

The international foot is defined as exactly 0.3048 meter. To convert meters to feet, divide by 0.3048, or multiply by about 3.28084. For example, 1.80 m ÷ 0.3048 = 5.9055 ft, so a height of 1.80 m is about 5 ft 11 in. The final rounded value is convenient for everyday reading; keep more digits during intermediate calculations if precision matters.

2. Convert kilograms to pounds

The avoirdupois pound is exactly 0.45359237 kg. To convert kilograms to pounds, divide by that factor, or multiply by about 2.20462. For example, 70 kg × 2.20462 = 154.3234 lb, commonly rounded to 154.3 lb. To reverse the conversion, multiply pounds by 0.45359237. Notice the direction: because a pound is less than a kilogram, the number of pounds is larger than the number of kilograms for the same mass.

3. Convert Celsius and Fahrenheit

Temperature scales use both an offset and a different step size, so do not convert them by multiplying alone. The formulas are:

  • °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32
  • °C = (°F − 32) × 5/9

For a worked example, 20 °C × 9/5 + 32 = 68 °F. To convert back, (68 − 32) × 5/9 = 20 °C. The 32-degree offset explains why 0 °C is not 0 °F.

4. Check which gallon a source means

“Gallon” is not one universal volume. A U.S. liquid gallon is about 3.785412 liters; an Imperial gallon used in the United Kingdom and some other contexts is 4.54609 liters. An Imperial gallon is about 20 percent larger. If a fuel listing or recipe simply says “gallon,” check its country or source before converting. For example, 10 U.S. gallons is about 37.85 L, while 10 Imperial gallons is 45.46 L. The difference is large enough to change a comparison.

5. Use a quick checking routine

  1. Name the quantity. Length, mass, temperature and volume need different rules.
  2. Confirm the exact unit. Check whether a source means U.S. customary or Imperial units.
  3. Set the direction. Decide which unit you have and which one you need.
  4. Estimate first. A meter is a little over three feet; a kilogram is a little over two pounds.
  5. Round at the end. Preserve useful digits in the calculation, then round for the task.

A metric and Imperial converter is especially useful when comparing travel distances, cooking volumes, package sizes or temperature settings. Conversion Calculator Plus can keep frequent pairs in favourites and history, while its calculator panel handles expressions. Read the result with its unit label, and keep separate measurements separate: a mass conversion does not tell you a volume unless you also know the material’s density.

A refresh may fail, in which case the app keeps the previously accepted rate and timestamp.

  4. Open the converter once before you go offline. This confirms that the app has the data you expect and gives you a chance to fix a missing currency pair or stale cache.

Read an offline quote correctly

Suppose the saved quote says 1 USD = 1.35 CAD. Entering 100 USD would show 135 CAD. This is an illustrative calculation, not a current market quote or a promise about what a card purchase will cost. If the rate was saved yesterday, it remains yesterday’s reference until the app successfully refreshes. The app’s result is a conversion estimate based on that saved quote, not a bank’s executed exchange rate.

Your bank, card network, ATM operator or cash-exchange desk may apply a different rate, a foreign-transaction fee, a cash advance charge or another service fee. A merchant may also offer to charge your card in your home currency; that choice can use a separate conversion rate. For the amount that will actually post to an account, review the provider’s terms and transaction record. A converter should help you compare and budget, not forecast a future exchange rate or guarantee a final charge.

Use it as a travel calculator

For a quick purchase check, enter the amount in the currency shown on the price tag, then read the converted result and its currency label. Try a few common amounts before shopping so you have a feel for the scale. Save frequently used pairs in favourites, and use conversion history to revisit a value. The expression calculator can also help with a simple total, such as multiplying a local price by the number of items, before you convert.

Conversion Calculator Plus works on iPhone and iPad and lets you open ordinary converters, Currency+, favourites and saved history without a connection. Refreshing rates and fetching charts that have not been loaded still require a connection. Premium includes widgets and Siri shortcuts if those fit your routine; the core offline usefulness comes from data already saved on the device. Check the timestamp, keep the quote’s limitations in mind, and use your bank or card statement for the amount actually charged.

Explore your loaded charts

Currency History lets you inspect a pair across short and long time ranges. One-finger taps and drags select a recorded rate. Current chart controls include pinch zoom on both axes, two-finger panning and double-tap reset. Read the Currency+ and Currency History guide for the full controls and minute-refresh details.

title: Engineering Unit Conversions: Pressure, Torque, Power and Data
description: A practical guide to pressure in pascals, kilopascals and bar; torque versus energy; watts versus watt-hours; and decimal versus binary data units.
body:
Engineering notes, product specifications and dashboards often mix unit systems. A conversion calculator can translate the number, but a correct interpretation starts with the quantity being measured. Pressure is not torque, power is not energy, and a decimal gigabyte is not the same size as a gibibyte. Use the following examples as unit literacy, then confirm any design limits or operating requirements with the responsible technical source.

Pressure: Pa, kPa and bar

The pascal (Pa) is the SI unit of pressure and equals one newton per square meter. A kilopascal is 1,000 pascals, and one bar equals 100,000 pascals, or 100 kPa. These relationships make conversion straightforward:

  • 250 kPa × 1,000 = 250,000 Pa
  • 250 kPa ÷ 100 = 2.5 bar

When comparing gauges, reports or equipment labels, also check whether the value is absolute pressure or gauge pressure. Converting units does not resolve that distinction, and a numerical match does not establish that a component is suitable for a particular application.

Torque is a turning effect

Torque describes a rotational effect: a force applied at a distance from an axis. Its common SI unit is the newton meter (N·m). Energy and work also have the dimensions of force times distance, and one joule is one newton meter in unit terms. Yet torque and energy describe different quantities, so torque should be written as N·m rather than relabeled as joules. For example, a specification of 12 N·m describes torque; it does not mean that 12 J of work was necessarily performed. The result depends on how the force and rotation act in the actual system.

Power is a rate; watt-hours are energy

A watt (W) measures power, or energy transferred per unit time: 1 W = 1 J/s. A watt-hour (Wh) measures energy over time. For a simple arithmetic example, a device operating at a steady 60 W for half an hour uses 30 Wh, because 60 W × 0.5 h = 30 Wh. Since one hour is 3,600 seconds, 30 Wh is 108,000 J, or 108 kJ. Keep the quantity and time interval attached to the answer; a watt value alone is not an energy total.

Data: GB and GiB

Storage and data-transfer descriptions may use decimal SI prefixes or binary prefixes. One gigabyte (GB) is 1,000,000,000 bytes. One gibibyte (GiB) is 1,073,741,824 bytes, or 230 bytes. A GB is therefore smaller than a GiB. Similarly, MB means 1,000,000 bytes while MiB means 1,048,576 bytes. If two specifications appear to disagree, check whether one uses decimal units and the other binary units before assuming the capacity changed.

A practical workflow is to write down the quantity, preserve its unit symbol, convert to the requested unit, and check the magnitude against an estimate. Conversion Calculator Plus includes pressure, torque, power and data categories among its unit conversions, with favourites and history for recurring values. It is an arithmetic aid: use current drawings, standards and manufacturer documentation for project decisions, and never infer safety or compliance from a converted number alone.

BIPM SI Brochure: The International System of Units
NIST: Definitions of the SI Units — Binary Prefixes
NIST Technical Note 938, Recommended Practice for the Use of Metric (SI) Units in Building Design and Construction

title: Measurement conversions: length, weight, temperature and engineering
description: Choose the right units for height, mass, area, volume, fuel, pressure, speed, energy, power and storage.
body:
A measurement converter starts with the quantity: length, weight, temperature, area and volume each use their own units. A measurement conversion calculator can make the arithmetic quick, but first check the unit system and the direction of conversion. Conversion Calculator Plus is a unit conversion calculator with everyday and engineering categories. Its complete directory lists every supported unit and symbol.

Whether you search for a units converter, measurements conversion calculator or units conversion calculator, the practical task is the same: convert units within the matching category. Unit conversion and unit conversions refer to this process; measurement conversion describes the same step for measured quantities. An offline unit converter can use fixed measurement relationships without downloading a market rate. Currency is different because current quotes need a connection.

Metric conversion and length

A metric conversion calculator or metric unit converter translates between named metric units and supported units from other systems. As a metric converter or metric calculator, the app can handle a measured value rather than guess what the original unit meant. A length converter and height converter use the Length category. For a height conversion calculator, check whether the source is centimeters, meters, inches or feet before entering it.

Length taskUnits to selectPractical check
cm to inches / cm to inches converterCentimeter → InchRead the result as decimal inches.
inches to cm / millimeters to inchesInch → Centimeter, or Millimeter → InchAn inches converter or inches unit converter needs a specified destination.
meters to feet converterMeter → FeetKeep feet distinct from inches.
cm to feet / cm to feet converterCentimeter → FeetUse the desired display precision.

A feet and inches converter converts between separately selected length units. Searches for a feet inch calculator, feet and inches calculator or inch calculator sometimes mean construction arithmetic using mixed notation such as 5 ft 11 in. Here, use explicit decimal inputs: compute 5 × 12 + 11 to obtain 71 inches, then convert the result. An automatic mixed-notation parser or construction solver is not promised. A footage conversion calculator likewise needs you to distinguish linear feet from square feet.

Weight conversion calculator

For a weight calculator, weight converter or weight unit converter, select the Weight category and the precise mass unit. A kg to lb weight converter and kg to lbs converter use kilograms as the input and pounds as the output. A lbs to kg converter reverses those selections. Pounds to kilograms and kilograms to pounds are opposite directions, so read both labels before using the answer.

Grams to ounces, a grams to ounces converter, and ounces to grams are mass comparisons. An ordinary ounce and a troy ounce differ. For ml to oz, volume units are needed instead; choose fluid ounces rather than a mass ounce. A converted weight alone does not tell you an ingredient’s volume.

Temperature converter

A celsius to fahrenheit converter and a fahrenheit to celsius converter handle temperature readings, including the offset between the scales. Choose the Thermal category for Celsius to Fahrenheit or Fahrenheit to Celsius. The app can serve as a celsius converter, fahrenheit converter or temperature calculator by selecting those input and output units. A temperature conversion calculator must distinguish a reading from an interval.

For a quick celsius fahrenheit check, 20 °C corresponds to 68 °F. The celsius fahrenheit conversion uses °F = °C × 9/5 + 32; reverse it with °C = (°F − 32) × 5/9. A celsius fahrenheit converter, fahrenheit celsius converter or celsius fahrenheit calculator should therefore account for the offset. Use the separate Temperature Interval category for a change in temperature rather than a thermometer reading.

Area and volume: work out dimensions first

An area conversion calculator, square meter converter or square feet converter translates an existing area. For an area calculator or square footage calculator task, first calculate a rectangle’s area as length × width with both measurements in the same unit. A square feet calculator then has a square-foot value to convert. The app does not measure a room from a photo or automatically solve a shape.

A volume calculator similarly starts with a known volume or a volume you have worked out from dimensions. Use a volume converter for liters to gallons or gallons to liters. A liters to gallons converter and gallons to liters converter must name US liquid or Imperial gallons because they differ. These tools translate the resulting quantity; they do not infer a container’s shape or fill level.

Engineering unit converter

An engineering converter covers several distinct quantities. Use a pressure converter or pressure unit converter for psi to bar and bar to psi. A torque converter here means a unit conversion for turning moment, rather than an automotive component. For a speed converter, mph to kph, kph to mph, kmh to mph and mph to kmh all require the matching mile-per-hour and kilometer-per-hour units.

An energy conversion calculator or energy unit converter uses the Energy category. An energy converter and energy calculator compare energy amounts. A power converter, power unit converter or power calculator uses Power instead. Power is energy per time, so a watt-hour is energy and a watt is power. Keep the quantity attached to the answer instead of treating the names as interchangeable.

Fuel and data storage

A fuel converter or mpg converter must distinguish US and Imperial gallons and direct fuel economy from fuel consumption. Use the exact unit shown by the vehicle specification. A data storage converter or bytes converter must distinguish decimal and binary units: mb to gb and gb to mb commonly refer to megabytes and gigabytes, whereas MiB and GiB denote binary units. Bits and bytes also differ, and Data Transfer Rate describes an amount per time rather than storage capacity.

For repeat conversions, keep favorites and review history. Inspect the complete catalog for specialist electrical, thermal, flow and radiation categories, as well as shoe and ring sizing scales. Conversion translates a value; it does not by itself validate a design or measurement.

title: Cooking and baking unit conversions
description: Convert cooking mass and volume while keeping density, cup sizes and gallon systems clear.
body:
A cooking unit converter helps when a recipe uses a different measurement system from your tools. Conversion Calculator Plus can be a kitchen unit converter for mass and volume: choose the quantity, select the named units and enter the amount. It also includes arithmetic for working out an amount before conversion. Cooking conversion is most dependable when every number keeps its unit label.

Cooking measurements: mass versus volume

A cooking conversion calculator or cooking converter can translate grams to ounces within mass, or milliliters to fluid ounces within volume. A kitchen converter does not make grams and milliliters interchangeable. To cross between them, you need the ingredient’s density and an appropriate measurement method. A gram of flour does not occupy the same volume as a gram of water.

If you use a kitchen calculator or cooking calculator to combine quantities, first put them in the same unit. For example, convert both mass values to grams before adding them. Keep a liquid volume separate from an ingredient mass unless you have an independently known density. The app’s Weight and Volume categories make that choice explicit.

Cups, ounces, quarts and liters

A cups to ounces converter means cups to fluid ounces when you are comparing volumes. Select the named cup standard and the corresponding fluid-ounce system rather than assuming every cup is identical. An ounces to ml converter likewise needs fluid ounces; oz to ml and fluid ounces to ml refer to volume only when that unit is specified. The shorthand ml to oz can otherwise confuse volume with mass.

A quart converter needs a named source system, just like a gallon converter. US customary and Imperial quantities differ. Liters to gallons and gallons to liters should therefore identify which gallon is used. These choices matter even before rounding the numerical result. Use the full unit catalog to inspect the available volume names and symbols.

Baking calculator and bakery conversions

As a baking calculator, the expression panel can multiply a known ingredient quantity before a unit conversion. A bakery unit converter or bakery converter then translates the result to another unit within the same category. For example, doubling an amount measured in grams remains a mass calculation; it does not automatically create an equivalent number of cups.

A recipe converter can mean a whole-recipe scaling tool, ingredient-density database or serving-size planner. This app covers unit conversion and arithmetic on entered quantities. It does not automatically rewrite a recipe, infer ingredient densities or adjust cooking time. When using it to support a recipe, scale each known amount deliberately, then convert within mass or volume as appropriate.

A repeatable kitchen workflow

  1. Read the recipe’s exact unit, including its region where relevant.
  2. Choose Weight for mass or Volume for liquid and container measures.
  3. Use arithmetic for a known multiplier, then inspect the converted amount.
  4. Round only as much as the measuring tool and recipe permit.
  5. Save frequent converter pairs in favorites and return to conversion history when checking earlier work.

Fixed measurement conversions can be useful offline. No currency quote is needed to compare grams with ounces or liters with a named gallon. Check the temperature category separately for oven temperature readings and remember that a temperature interval is a different quantity from a reading.

Exchange rate calculator and FX names

An exchange rate is the relationship between two currencies at a particular time. An exchange rate calculator, exchange rates calculator or exchange calculator applies that relationship to an amount. Currency exchange rates, a currency exchange rate and currency rates all need a source time and a direction. Exchange rates can be saved or dated even if the app was opened recently.

Forex means foreign exchange. A forex calculator, fx calculator, forex converter, forex currency converter or foreign exchange calculator here compares currency amounts. The app does not place forex orders or calculate a broker’s pip value, margin requirement or position risk. Money exchange happens with a bank or other provider, not through this converter. title: How to use Siri and Shortcuts with Conversion Calculator Plus
description: Set up Siri, convert units by voice, run saved converters, update widgets and build an Apple shortcut with Conversion Calculator Plus.
body:
Use Siri with Conversion Calculator Plus to convert units, run a saved converter or change the amount shown by a saved converter’s widgets. You can also use the same actions in Apple’s Shortcuts app. The English spoken app name in the examples is Convert Plus.

Before you start: Siri conversions and interactive widgets require an active Premium subscription. The examples below use English; speech recognition and available phrases depend on Siri’s language. Translated commands need their own device checks.

Set up the app and Siri

  1. Install or update Conversion Calculator Plus, then open it once so its actions and saved converters can become available to Siri.
  2. Check your Premium access in the app. If you already subscribed but access is missing, use Restore Purchases and reopen the app.
  3. In your device’s Settings, find Siri or Apple Intelligence & Siri. Enable voice activation, or use your device’s Siri button shortcut. Menu names vary with iOS.
  4. For these English examples, choose an English Siri language. In the app, open Settings → Siri → Using Siri for its illustrated conversation tutorial.

You can begin with a one-off conversion. A saved converter or Home Screen widget is not needed for that route.

Convert units without saving a converter

Say “Hey Siri, convert with Convert Plus.” Answer the prompts in this order:

  1. Amount: “10.”
  2. Category: “Length.”
  3. From unit: “Meters.”
  4. To unit: “Feet.”

Siri returns the conversion result. Prompt wording and number formatting may differ from this example. The category helps distinguish names that occur in different kinds of measurement. Use complete names such as “square meter” or “meter per second” when appropriate.

To start another conversion, say “Hey Siri, convert another with Convert Plus.” This starts a new action; it does not automatically carry over the previous category and units.

Save a converter for a conversion you repeat

A short, distinctive name lets you request the unit pair without speaking both units each time.

  1. Open Widgets in the app; it is also available through Settings.
  2. Tap Create converter.
  3. Enter Meters to Feet as the name.
  4. Choose Length, with Meter as the source and Feet as the destination.
  5. Set a starting amount and tap Save converter.

Say “Hey Siri, run Meters to Feet in Convert Plus.” Siri asks for the amount to convert. Replace “Meters to Feet” with your saved name if you chose something else.

You can instead say “Hey Siri, run a saved conversion in Convert Plus.” and choose the converter when asked. Running a saved conversion calculates the amount you supply; it does not change the saved widget amount. Saving the converter is enough for this Siri action—you do not have to place a widget on the Home Screen.

Try a one-off conversion, then save the pair you use most often. Siri actions require Premium.

View Conversion Calculator Plus on the App Store ↗

Change a Home Screen widget’s amount by voice

To see the result on your Home Screen, add a Conversion+ widget. Touch and hold the placed widget, choose Edit Widget and select the saved converter you created.

Say “Hey Siri, use Convert Plus to update Meters to Feet.” When Siri asks for the new amount, say “25.” This action updates the saved amount and requests a widget refresh. Every widget using that saved converter receives the change; the time it appears is managed by iOS.

Siri identifies the converter by its saved name, not its Home Screen position. Use separate saved converters, such as “Travel Length” and “Work Length,” when voice updates should affect different groups of widgets.

Build a shortcut using the app’s actions

In Apple’s Shortcuts app, find Conversion Calculator Plus under App Shortcuts. Its tiles include Convert Units, Convert Saved and Set Widget Amount. The saved-conversion action’s fuller editor title is Convert with Saved Converter.

  1. Create a new shortcut with the + button and name it My Length Check.
  2. Open the action picker and search for Convert with Saved Converter. Select the action belonging to Conversion Calculator Plus.
  3. Choose Meters to Feet for Saved Converter and enter 10 for Amount.
  4. Add Apple’s Show Result action and use the conversion action’s returned value as its input.
  5. Run the shortcut in the editor and check the displayed result, then finish saving it.

Activate Siri and say “My Length Check.” This runs your custom shortcut with its configured amount. Edit Amount to change it. Apple documents creating shortcuts and running them by name with Siri; control labels vary between iOS versions.

If Siri cannot find the action or stays silent

  • Action missing: update and open the app, then look in Shortcuts for the app’s actions. Try running the action there to separate setup problems from voice recognition.
  • Wrong saved converter: check the exact saved name and avoid duplicate names. Use the generic saved-conversion command to choose one.
  • Units misunderstood: use a named saved converter to avoid repeating ambiguous unit names.
  • No spoken reply: in Siri settings, find Responses or Siri Responses and select the spoken-response option, such as Prefer Spoken Responses. iOS controls speech output.

See the calculator, history and widgets guide for related workflows, and the complete category and unit catalog when choosing a conversion.
